OVERVIEW

Costco is a membership-warehouse retailer. It describes its model as: "We operate membership warehouses and e-commerce sites based on the concept that offering low prices on a limited selection of nationally-branded and private-label products in a wide range of categories will produce high sales volumes and rapid inventory turnover." [10-K.txt:L180] The warehouse base was "939, 914, and 890 warehouses worldwide at August 30, 2026, August 31, 2025, and September 1, 2024." [10-K.txt:L177] Management says the model depends on limited selection: "We carry less than 4,000 active stock keeping units (SKUs) per warehouse in our core warehouse business, significantly less than other broadline retailers." [10-K.txt:L187]

The reported scale for fiscal 2026 (52 weeks ended August 30, 2026) is "Net sales increased 10% to $297,247, driven by an increase in comparable sales and sales at new warehouses;" [10-K.txt:L709] and "Net income increased 14% to $9,226, $20.76 per diluted share, compared to $8,099, $18.21 per diluted share in 2025; and" [10-K.txt:L721]. The earnings release says "Net sales for the quarter increased 11.2 percent, to $93.9 billion, from $84.4 billion last year." [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L10]

I treat management's growth as a claim to test. Three features of the business shape that test.
- Revenue concentration is high: "Our financial and operational performance is highly dependent on our U.S. and Canadian operations, which comprised 86% and 83% of net sales and operating income in 2026." [10-K.txt:L350] Within the U.S., "we are highly dependent on our California operations, which comprised 26% of U.S. net sales in 2026." [10-K.txt:L350]
- International is smaller but more profitable per sales dollar: "During 2026, our international operations, including Canada, generated 27% and 35% of our net sales and operating income." [10-K.txt:L407]
- Supplier concentration is not a stated issue: "We do not obtain a significant portion of merchandise from any one supplier." [10-K.txt:L211]

Gasoline adds sales but dilutes margin. "Our gasoline business represented 11% of total net sales in 2026." [10-K.txt:L207] "A higher penetration of gasoline sales will generally lower our gross margin percentage." [10-K.txt:L693]

MARKET POSITIONING AND GROWTH OUTLOOK

Criterion 1, Demand durability: SUPPORTED.
- Comparable sales growth came from both ticket and traffic. "Comparable sales were positively impacted by increases of 5% in average ticket and 3% in shopping frequency." [10-K.txt:L835] The earnings release shows fiscal-year total-company comparable sales of "8.4%" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L36] and "6.6%" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L37] on the adjusted basis, which excludes gasoline-price and foreign-exchange effects.
- The core categories drove most of the growth. "Sales increased $17,136 or 8% in core merchandise categories, increasing in all categories." [10-K.txt:L837]
- Gasoline price inflation inflated reported sales, so the headline overstates organic growth. "Higher gasoline prices positively impacted net sales by $3,501, or 130 basis points, and changes in foreign currencies positively impacted net sales by $1,332, or 49 basis points;" [10-K.txt:L711] Gasoline volume was also up: "The volume of gasoline sold increased 7%, positively impacting net sales by $1,913, or 71 basis points." [10-K.txt:L838]
- Membership counts rose. Paid members were "84,100" at the end of 2026 [10-K.txt:L223] against "81,000" in 2025 [10-K.txt:L224]. Total cardholders were "150,400" [10-K.txt:L231] against "145,200" [10-K.txt:L232].
- Executive members were "42,300, 38,700, and 35,400 of total paid members in 2026, 2025, and 2024." [10-K.txt:L237] "The penetration of sales to Executive members represented approximately 75.2% of worldwide net sales in 2026." [10-K.txt:L237]
- Renewal was strong: "Our member renewal rate was 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada and 89.8% worldwide at the end of 2026." [10-K.txt:L238]
- Membership fee revenue was "Membership fee revenue increased 11% to $5,907, driven by new member sign-ups, membership fee increases, and upgrades to Executive membership;" [10-K.txt:L713]
- One caution: management states that "Our worldwide renewal rate is adversely impacted by membership growth in certain international markets and a higher penetration of memberships sold online, including through digital membership promotions, which renew at a slightly lower rate on average." [10-K.txt:L695]
- Digital demand is growing quickly: "Digitally-enabled comparable sales increased 21% during 2026, both as reported and excluding the impact of changes in foreign currencies." [10-K.txt:L836]

Criterion 2, Competitive position: MIXED.
- Management names the competition: "Walmart, Target, Kroger, and Amazon are among our significant general merchandise retail competitors in the U.S." [10-K.txt:L275] The supplied filings give no peer-level share or pricing data, so a claimed advantage over named competitors is not established by the supplied evidence.
- Operating measures are supportive but not uniformly so. In core categories, "The gross margin in core merchandise categories when expressed as a percentage of their own sales increased 15 basis points." [10-K.txt:L885] Company-wide, "Excluding the impact of gasoline price inflation on net sales, gross margin percentage was 11.22%, an increase of 10 basis points." [10-K.txt:L884]
- Reported gross margin percentage was slightly lower at "11.09" [10-K.txt:L878] against "11.12" in 2025 [10-K.txt:L880].
- Cost leverage depends on gasoline. "SG&A expenses as a percentage of net sales decreased 10 basis points compared to 2025." [10-K.txt:L905] Excluding gasoline, "SG&A expenses as a percentage of net sales excluding the impact of gasoline price inflation was 9.26%, an increase of one basis point." [10-K.txt:L905] SG&A also "increased in our Canadian and Other International segments and were flat in our U.S. segment compared to 2025." [10-K.txt:L905]
- Private label is cited as a differentiator: "We expect to continue to increase the sales penetration of our private-label items." [10-K.txt:L277]
- Management flags competitive risk from AI and technology: "Some competitors have greater technology capabilities, including the faster adoption of AI technologies, and greater market penetration than we do." [10-K.txt:L395]

FUTURE DEVELOPMENTS AND STRATEGIC RECOMMENDATIONS

Criterion 3, Growth execution: SUPPORTED, with cost and cannibalization caveats.
- Openings are on pace. "We opened 28 new warehouses, including three relocations, for a total of 25 net new warehouses: 18 in the U.S., five in our Canadian segment, and two in our Other International segment, compared to 27 new warehouses, including three relocations, in 2025;" [10-K.txt:L707]
- The plan is larger for 2027: management plans to "and plan to open up to 33 new warehouses, including five relocations, in 2027." [10-K.txt:L1018]
- Capital spending is rising. Additions to property and equipment were "(6,435)" in 2026 [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L310] against "(5,498)" in 2025 [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L311]. Management states "our current intention to spend approximately $7,500 du" [10-K.txt:L1009] for fiscal "2027" [10-K.txt:L1011], and "These expenditures are expected to be financed with cash from operations, cash and cash equivalents, and short-term investments." [10-K.txt:L1013]
- Funding capacity is evident: "Net cash provided by operating activities totaled $15,817 in 2026, compared to $13,335 in 2025." [10-K.txt:L1000] "Cash and cash equivalents and short-term investments were $21,301 and $15,284 at August 30, 2026, and August 31, 2025." [10-K.txt:L989]
- Data inconsistency: the earnings release shows operating cash flow of "15,825" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L306], not the 10-K's $15,817. The release statements are labeled "Subject to Reclassification" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L277]. I rely on the 10-K figure.
- The cost of expansion is acknowledged: "Negative aspects of such growth include lower initial operating profitability relative to existing warehouses and cannibalization of sales at existing warehouses when openings occur in existing markets." [10-K.txt:L694] Management expects international to keep outpacing: "Our rate of square footage growth is generally higher in many of our international markets, due to the smaller base in those markets, and we expect that to continue." [10-K.txt:L694]
- Labor cost is part of the expansion bill. "At the end of 2026, we employed 355,000 employees worldwide." [10-K.txt:L244] Management also states "In March 2026, we increased the top of wage scales by $1.00 per hour in the U.S. and Canada" [10-K.txt:L270].
- The effectiveness of supply-chain investments is less certain: "The effectiveness of these investments can be less predictable than opening new locations and might not provide the anticipated benefits or desired rates of return." [10-K.txt:L357]

Catalysts and recent developments.
- IEEPA tariff refunds. "During 2026, we began filing for refunds and received $184, made up of $174 in refunds, recorded as a reduction to merchandise costs, and $10 recorded as interest income." [10-K.txt:L726] After year-end, "Subsequent to 2026, we received $155 in additional refunds and we intend to continue to invest the majority of the refunds in increased value for the member." [10-K.txt:L726] The refunds flattered the fourth quarter: "This year's fourth quarter was positively impacted by a non-recurring benefit of $0.15 per diluted share from IEEPA tariff refunds received in the quarter, less partial reinvestment of those refunds in increased member values." [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L44]
- Shareholder returns. "In April, the Board of Directors approved a 13% increase in the quarterly cash dividend." [10-K.txt:L723]
- Debt maturity. The current portion of long-term debt is "2,248" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L227] against "75" a year earlier [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L228].
- Expectations risk. "We believe that the price of our stock currently reflects high market expectations for our future operating results." [10-K.txt:L417]

Strategic recommendations, framed as monitoring priorities for an investor.
1. Judge the thesis on organic demand, not headline sales. Gasoline-price inflation added 130 basis points to 2026 net sales [10-K.txt:L711], so focus on the adjusted comparable sales figure of "6.6%" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L37] and on ticket versus frequency.
2. Watch whether the planned openings, up to 33 in 2027 [10-K.txt:L1018], dilute existing-warehouse performance, given the cannibalization risk in [10-K.txt:L694].
3. Expect the tariff refund to be non-recurring. The $0.15 per diluted share benefit [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L44] should not be treated as run-rate earnings.
4. Monitor concentration in the U.S., Canada and California [10-K.txt:L350] as the main downside exposure.

What would change my view. My strongest conclusion is that demand is durable. The measure that would challenge it is the worldwide renewal rate in the next 10-K. It was "89.8% worldwide" at the end of 2026 [10-K.txt:L238], and management already says online and international sign-ups renew at lower rates [10-K.txt:L695]. A worldwide renewal rate below 89.8% would indicate that paid-member growth from "81,000" to "84,100" [10-K.txt:L224, L223] is being bought with lower-quality sign-ups. That would weaken the demand-durability conclusion. Management itself says renewal rates "materially influence" profitability [10-K.txt:L695].

Insight: Membership fee revenue rose 11% to $5,907 in 2026, but the fee increase explained only about 30% of that growth versus about 40% in 2025, so a growing share of membership income growth came from other drivers named in the filing, such as sign-ups and Executive upgrades. [10-K.txt:L854] "As previously reported, we increased annual membership fees in the U.S. and Canada, effective September 1, 2024. We account for membership fee revenue on a deferred basis, recognized ratably over the one-year membership period. The fee income increase accounted for approximately 30% and 40% of membership income growth during 2026 and 2025."
